channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: A code-native newspaper of meaningful software change.

item.title: Direct Reports Drive Anthropic’s Growing Vulnerability Count
item.description: The company’s disclosure total has more than doubled since August. Most of the net increase sits in the route without the same external review—a useful distinction when judging what the expanding program delivers.

item.title: Hugging Face Adds Task-by-Task Browsing for Agent Benchmarks
item.description: Harbor’s executable tests now fit the ordinary dataset viewer and loading tools. Evaluators can inspect instructions and declared requirements together before choosing which work to run.

item.title: Git Adds Squashing Without Switching Branches
item.description: The experimental history editor can fold an older patch series while leaving a separate working branch alone. Its handling of dependent branches—and some merges—defines the useful new choice.

item.title: ChatGPT Plugins Can Now Start Work from App Events
item.description: OpenAI’s new event subscriptions give plugin builders a way to describe what should start a job. The useful change is an explicit integration contract for ongoing work, with the app still responsible for getting its events delivered.

item.title: Pi Adds Built-In MCP—and Keeps the Tools Replaceable
item.description: The coding agent once left MCP to outside extensions. Its new release supplies an implementation, while giving extension authors a shared way to call tools and the ability to replace the defaults.

item.title: Inside TypeSafe’s Model Comparison: What the Adapter Makes You Pay For
item.description: A probability-bearing answer buys more than a label. Local decision models and a public routing experiment now expose the next choice: how much accuracy must the cheaper route preserve?

item.title: Who Supplies the Agent? OpenAI Hosts It, Pydantic Assembles It
item.description: Pydantic’s weekend changes tie a framework, a coding harness and a terminal client to one release process. Set beside OpenAI’s managed Agents API, they reveal a choice that model rankings miss: which parts of the agent your team still has to run.

item.title: API Discovery: Ask OpenWork Who Needs to Sign In
item.description: OpenWork’s new auth guide and discovery metadata let an agent distinguish starting a workspace from acting as its owner. Permission errors can now name the human handoff instead of inviting another retry.

item.title: Builder Work: The Example Config Was Taking Real Requests
item.description: OptiLLM stopped treating its bundled provider examples as an automatic fallback. A clean-directory test shows the difference—and why an empty provider list is not the end of a routing audit.

item.title: OpenClaw Retires the Ledger That Watched Its Other Ledgers
item.description: Tasks and TaskFlow are gone from OpenClaw’s main branch. Background execution remains, but plugins lose a shared interface—and some upgrade scenarios still lack a completed proof.

item.title: You Sent the Correction. Has the Agent Read It?
item.description: QM now places a mid-run correction where the agent runtime receives it. That small change separates a delivery problem from an agent that had the information and still went wrong.

item.title: API Discovery: Keep Talking When Memory Cannot Catch Up
item.description: Mastra adds a choice after memory-model retries run out. Continuing preserves the unprocessed input, so a long outage can still fill the agent’s context.

item.title: Builder Work: Give Extra Memory a Budget, Not the Whole Context
item.description: A Headlong review found that helpful citations could overwhelm a small context request—or stop it halfway through. The repair gives optional memory its own limits while preserving the base.

item.title: Unsloth’s Sandbox Is Back. A Working Tool Still Does Not Prove Isolation.
item.description: The replacement for Studio’s reverted sandbox has landed, followed by a Windows Preview. Its promise is conditional: establish what boundary actually ran, and distinguish an unavailable host from a launch that must be refused.

item.title: API Discovery: Find the Approval in the Right Ledger
item.description: Mastra’s HTTP approval flow could miss an Inngest-backed run and then deny its owner. A merged repair restores discovery without treating another user’s run as fair game.

item.title: Builder Work: Do Not Return a Tab Nobody Owns
item.description: Tangle’s move from a large React context to a shared store contains a sharper lesson than a library preference: an agent-facing creation method must not report an object that its owner never accepted.

item.title: Goose Gets Small Enough to Bundle. Its Old Recipes May Not Fit.
item.description: A lean agent build answers Buzz’s packaging problem. The review draws a harder line around which existing configurations it will carry.

item.title: API Discovery: A Timestamp Is Not a Heartbeat
item.description: Tangle now exposes when a container record was updated. Use it to explain an observation, without declaring an unchanged job dead.

item.title: Builder Work: Test the Tool Change at the Wire
item.description: LangChain’s AI-assisted integration shows why a tool definition needs tests for its position, its caller and its trip through the serializer.

item.title: Qwen Code Draws a New Sandbox Boundary. Saving the Policy Still Has a Gap.
item.description: Linux tool confinement now leaves the agent’s model connection on the host. The public review shows why the settings file that selects that boundary deserves just as much scrutiny.

item.title: API Discovery: Ask Which Skills Exist Before Guessing Their Names
item.description: OpenWork adds a direct, read-only route from a member’s permitted skill catalog to its instructions. The returned total matters as much as the list.

item.title: Builder Work: A Redaction Test That Had Never Written a Note
item.description: Headlong’s privacy fix gained a stronger test only after review noticed that the supposedly protected memory file never existed.

item.title: The Approval Arrived. The Subagent Could Not Continue.
item.description: Microsoft’s Agent Framework closes a misleading route through delegated tool approval. A child can decide immediately under policy; a person who answers later needs a workflow that knows where to return.

item.title: API Discovery: Shorten the Context, Keep the History
item.description: Pi v0.87.0 lets a builder append an edit to future model context while leaving the original transcript intact. That is useful for a reading assistant—and it is not data deletion.

item.title: Builder Work: The Last Writer Is Not the Last Run
item.description: CrewAI’s new evaluation shortcut needs a trustworthy pointer to completed work. The hard part is deciding which run deserves the file when exports and writers arrive out of order.

item.title: Jev puts the odds in the answer. Local AI still has to make them trustworthy.
item.description: TypeSafe's new decision model makes probabilities part of the interface. Ollama's long-requested logprobs already shipped—but reading a token's likelihood and trusting an automated decision are different engineering problems.

item.title: OpenClaw Had Stopped the Child. Restart Brought Back the Parent.
item.description: A waiting conversation could survive its own cancellation in OpenClaw’s recovery records. A new repair saves the parent’s stopped state before answering the user—and protects a newer turn from that delayed write.

item.title: API Discovery: Let the Agent Pick a Record You Already Have
item.description: Pydantic AI’s new Choices helper builds a menu from data available at run time. The model selects a validated key; the application gets back the record that key represents.

item.title: Builder Work: No Score Is a Result Worth Preserving
item.description: Mastra’s agent-assisted evaluation work gives an irrelevant run a separate outcome. The difficult part is carrying that distinction all the way to storage, averages and the final verdict.

item.title: Qwen Code Stops Calling a Rerun a Resume
item.description: Two September 18 changes separate a recoverable interruption from a fresh start: refuse a missing journal, then make the interrupted run visible. Neither promises automatic recovery.
